name: Surface exploration drilling
summary: To find the next ounces near the mine, exploration geologists drill diamond core holes from surface into targets picked in the annual program. For each hole a project geologist plans the collar and direction, checks claims and permits, lays out access, supervises the contract rig that drills around the clock, decides when to stop, checks the downhole survey and certifies the metres for payment. Holes are slowed by waiting for a free rig, by freeze-up and break-up that decide when swampy ground can be reached, by permits for new areas, and by lost or deviated holes that must be redrilled.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine northern Ontario gold producer running near-mine and Quebec surface programs of tens of thousands of metres a year with contract diamond drills.
baseline.notes: One case is one surface hole from planning to the approved contractor certificate. Core logging and sampling are a separate process.

trigger: The exploration program releases the next target for drilling.
end_state: The hole is drilled, surveyed, closed and recorded, the core is at the core shack and the contractor's metres are certified for payment.

volume.seasonality: Peak from January to March on frozen ground; a pause on swampy targets during spring break-up in April and May; steady through summer and fall on dry ground.

evidence.note: Reference 2021 guidance of 54,000 m surface at the mine and 42,000 m in Quebec; a comparable mine averaged about 870 m per surface hole, while near-mine holes here are assumed at 300-600 m, giving roughly 10-25 holes a month.

surge.cause: winter drilling season on frozen ground

evidence.note: Organisation file surge; swampy targets are drilled after freeze-up in January to March.
Hands-on time per hole in this file is about 19 hours for the project geologists, about 285 hours a month at 15 holes. The five geologists also log core (a separate process).
Daily core pickup from the rigs, about 5-6 hours per hole including trips during extensions.
Claim and permit checks, permit applications and collar data entry.
Approves hole plans and contractor certificates.
Notifies communities of drilling under agreement commitments; not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: Mining Lands Administration System (Ontario) and GESTIM (Quebec) claim portals
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network

resources.name: Exploration pickup trucks, ATVs and snowmobiles

steps.name: Plan the hole
steps.description: The project geologist picks the next target from the approved program, opens the 3D model of the drill holes and geology, and sets the collar, azimuth, dip and target depth so the hole cuts the zone at the planned spacing. He writes a one-page hole plan with the expected depth and cost.

error.defect_description: Hole aimed at the wrong pierce point after a model update.

evidence.note: First-phase exploration holes at 50-100 m spacing at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Exploration manager approves the hole
steps.description: The exploration manager reviews the hole plan against the program budget, the metres left in the contract and the priority of other targets, and approves it or asks for a change of target or depth.

error.defect_description: Approved over budget without noting it.

control.basis: Exploration budget authority: manager approval of each hole

evidence.note: Hole-by-hole approval is common in programs run by an exploration manager.

steps.name: Check claim and permit coverage
steps.description: The database geologist checks in the claims portal and the permit files that the collar and the hole trace sit on claims in good standing and inside an approved exploration permit area. Holes outside existing permits need an application before any rig moves.

error.defect_description: Permit boundary misread on the map.

evidence.note: Mechanized drilling with a drill over 150 kg needs an Ontario exploration permit, valid up to three years.

steps.name: Prepare the exploration permit application
steps.description: The database geologist fills in the exploration permit or plan application in the online system with the claims, activities, maps and rehabilitation plan, and submits it. He copies the community relations coordinator so communities hear about it from the company too.

error.defect_description: Application map omits a claim the hole crosses.

control.basis: Ontario Mining Act and Regulation 308/12: exploration plans and permits for early exploration

evidence.note: Permit applications are posted for comment under the Mining Act and Regulation 308/12.

steps.name: Wait for the ministry's permit decision
steps.description: The ministry posts the application, Indigenous communities and the public have 30 days to comment, and the ministry then issues or refuses the permit. Questions from the ministry or a community can extend the wait.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Ontario Mining Act: Crown consultation with Indigenous communities before an exploration permit decision

evidence.note: A 30-day comment period followed by issue two days later in the notice opened; the longer tail is the author's estimate for applications that draw concerns.

steps.name: Notify communities and landholders
steps.description: The community relations coordinator tells the First Nations under the company's agreements, and any surface rights holders or trappers, where and when drilling will start and how to raise concerns. He records the notice in the consultation log.

error.defect_description: A trapline holder is not told.

control.basis: Community agreement commitments on notice of exploration activity

evidence.note: Notification under community agreements; the organisation file lists Indigenous and community relations as a process.

steps.name: Travel to the collar site
steps.description: The project geologist drives a pickup from the camp or core shack and finishes by ATV or snowmobile, or on foot through bush, to the planned collar. Spring break-up and road restrictions can close access for days.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Bush access around a northern Ontario mine; break-up closures are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Spot the collar and lay out access
steps.description: The geologist locates the collar with a handheld GPS, flags it and the front and back sights for the azimuth, checks distances from water and trails against the permit conditions, and flags a route for the access trail and pad.

error.defect_description: Sights set on the wrong azimuth.

evidence.note: Surface collars are located and later surveyed by GPS at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Contractor builds the trail and drill pad
steps.description: A local contractor cuts and levels the access trail and drill pad, or floods and packs an ice road and pad on swampy ground once the ground has frozen. In fall and spring the work waits for freeze-up or for the ground to firm.

error.defect_description: Pad too small for the rig and water tank.

evidence.note: Contractor work time shown as elapsed wait; freeze-up timing from the organisation file's winter drilling surge.

steps.name: Wait for a rig to come free
steps.description: The hole waits until one of the contract rigs finishes its current hole. With three rigs on a program of this size the queue is usually one to two holes per rig.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Three surface rigs at the reference mine in 2021.

steps.name: Contractor moves and sets up the rig
steps.description: The drilling crew tears down at the last hole, moves the rig, water pump, lines and drill shack by skidder or truck, and sets up and aligns the rig on the sights. Winter moves on ice roads are faster than summer moves through bush.

error.defect_description: Rig aligned off the planned dip.

evidence.note: Surface drilling is contracted out at a comparable mine; move times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pre-start rig and site safety inspection
steps.description: The project geologist checks the rig alignment with a compass or alignment tool, walks the site with the drill foreman to check guarding, spill kits, fuel containment and the emergency plan, and signs the pre-start inspection before drilling starts.

error.defect_description: Spill containment gap not noticed.

control.basis: Company contractor safety program and drilling contract: pre-start inspection of rig and site

evidence.note: Pre-start inspections are standard in drilling contracts.

steps.name: Contractor drills the hole
steps.description: The drill crew drills NQ core around the clock on two 12-hour shifts, takes single-shot downhole surveys at intervals, and fills out a daily drill report with metres, hours and consumables. Ground problems, water loss or a breakdown slow it.

error.defect_description: Hole deviates off target or rods are lost.

evidence.note: NQ surface core and downhole surveys every 30 m at comparable mines; duration is the author's estimate for 300-600 m holes at roughly 60-110 m a day.

steps.name: Pick up core and deliver it to the core shack
steps.description: Each day a core technician drives to the rig, checks the core boxes are labelled and the depth blocks are in place, loads them and brings them to the core shack for logging. Over a hole this adds up to several trips.

error.defect_description: Boxes stacked out of order or lids lost in transit.

evidence.note: Daily core pickup at a rig within an hour of the core shack.

steps.name: Review drill reports and decide when to stop
steps.description: The project geologist reads the daily drill reports, checks metres and core recovery, visits the rig to look at core near the target, and decides whether to stop at planned depth, extend the hole, or re-collar a hole that was lost or deviated badly.

error.defect_description: Stopped short of the target zone.

evidence.note: Extension and lost-hole shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the end-of-hole survey
steps.description: The driller or a survey contractor runs a gyro survey down the full hole to record its path. The rig stays on the hole until the survey is done.

error.defect_description: Survey file has a tool misreading.

evidence.note: Surface holes surveyed by Reflex or gyro at comparable mines.

steps.name: Check the survey and approve hole closure
steps.description: The geologist loads the survey into the database software, checks for jumps or magnetic interference and that the hole reached the target, and tells the foreman to close the hole. A bad survey is rerun before the rods are pulled.

error.defect_description: Interference not noticed in the survey.

evidence.note: Survey practice at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Contractor closes the hole
steps.description: The crew pulls the rods, grouts or plugs the hole, leaves the casing capped and labelled with the hole number, and tears down. The rig is then free for the next hole.

error.defect_description: Casing left uncapped.

control.basis: Ontario Provincial Standards for Early Exploration: drill hole and site rehabilitation

evidence.note: Holes grouted when completed or abandoned at a comparable mine; permits require the Provincial Standards for Early Exploration.

steps.name: Inspect and rehabilitate the drill site
steps.description: The geologist inspects the site after the rig leaves, checks the sump, spills and garbage, photographs the capped casing and site, and has the contractor fix anything left. In winter final cleanup may wait for snowmelt.

error.defect_description: Hydrocarbon spill under snow missed.

control.basis: Ontario Mining Act exploration permit conditions and Provincial Standards for Early Exploration

evidence.note: Permit holders must meet the Provincial Standards for Early Exploration.

steps.name: Enter collar and hole data in the database
steps.description: The database geologist enters the collar coordinates, final depth, survey and dates into the drillhole database and flags the collar for a later GPS survey. The hole is then ready for logs and assays.

error.defect_description: Coordinates entered in the wrong datum.

evidence.note: Collars digitally surveyed at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Reconcile drill reports and prepare the contractor certificate
steps.description: At month end the project geologist adds up metres by size, hours for moves, standby and surveys, and consumables from the daily reports, compares them with the contract rates and the contractor's statement, and prepares the work certificate.

error.defect_description: Standby hours or metres double-counted.

evidence.note: Monthly certification of contract drilling, as the organisation file links this process to accounts payable.

steps.name: Exploration manager approves the certificate
steps.description: The exploration manager reviews the certificate against the program budget and the drill reports and approves it for payment, or queries unexplained standby or extra charges with the contractor.

error.defect_description: Overcharge approved.

control.basis: Company approval matrix: certificate prepared by the geologist and approved by the manager before payment

evidence.note: Approval workflow from general practice.

exceptions.name: New exploration permit needed
exceptions.description: The hole is outside existing permit areas and waits for a ministry decision after a 30-day comment period.

exceptions.name: Hole lost or badly deviated
exceptions.description: Rods are stuck or the hole wanders off target and the rig re-collars or wedges a new hole.

exceptions.name: Hole extended
exceptions.description: Mineralisation continues past the planned depth and the geologist extends the hole.

exceptions.name: Waiting for freeze-up
exceptions.description: Targets on swampy ground cannot be reached until ice roads and pads can be built.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from hole plan to approved contractor certificate
benchmarks.population: Surface exploration holes at a northern Ontario mine

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about a week to plan and prepare, a few days' wait for a rig, about a week of drilling and closing, a few days to record, and certification in the next month-end batch, which alone adds two weeks on average.

pain_points.description: Holes queue for one of three rigs, and rig moves and standby are paid whether or not the rig drills.

evidence.note: Three surface rigs at the reference mine; the queue is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Access to swampy targets depends on freeze-up and break-up, so the program is crowded into winter.

evidence.note: Organisation file winter surge.

pain_points.description: Metres, hours and consumables are added up by hand from paper daily drill reports at month end, and errors lead to queries with the contractor.

evidence.note: Paper drill reports were common in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Holes outside permitted areas wait at least a month for a permit decision.

evidence.note: 30-day comment period before an exploration permit decision.

sources.supports: Ontario early exploration permit notice: mechanized drilling with a drill over 150 kg and stripping or trenching need an exploration permit under the Mining Act; proposal posted for a 30-day comment period (26 September to 26 October 2025) with the permit issued 28 October; permit term up to three years with renewal; Indigenous communities and the public may comment; activities must follow Ontario Regulation 308/12 and the Provincial Standards for Early Exploration

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file. Drill contractor time is a contract cost: it is shown as elapsed wait (cause external_party, transit or weather) on external steps and as rig hours in the step resources, not as hands-on labour.

Rig capacity: in this file each hole holds a rig for about 190 hours (move, drilling including extensions, survey and closing). At the organisation file's 450 available hours a month per rig, three rigs complete about 7 holes a month, and 15 holes a month would need about six. The reference company drilled 54,000 m at the mine with three surface rigs in 2021 (about 1,500 m per rig a month, which needs about 600 rig hours a month at the drilling rates used here) and drilled another 42,000 m in Quebec with separate rigs. The organisation file's rig count of 3 and 450 available hours are therefore reported as too low for 15 holes a month; the simulated resource queue at step s10 assumes the practical rig count is closer to five.
Hole depth of 300-600 m for near-mine holes is the author's assumption; a comparable mine's directional surface holes averaged about 870 m.
The exploration permit wait and community notice apply to the Ontario property; Quebec work follows a similar but separate regime not modelled here.
Community relations coordinator takes part but is not listed for this process in the organisation file.
